'''Andrew John Orr-Ewing''' (born 1965)<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | title=Orr-Ewing, Prof. Andrew John | author=Anon|year=2017 |id = U289299 | doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.289299 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> is a British chemist and [[Professor]] of [[physical chemistry]] at the [[University of Bristol]]. His work investigates the mechanisms of [[chemical reaction]] in both the [[Phase (matter)|gas and liquid phases]] and has used [[ultrafast laser spectroscopy]] to observe the effects of [[solvent]]s on molecular reaction and the dynamics of [[photodissociation]].<ref name=googlescholar>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name=frs/><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref><ref name=epmc>{{EuropePMC|0000-0001-5551-9609}}</ref>

==Education==

Orr-Ewing was educated at [[Dr Challoner's Grammar School]]<ref name=whoswho/> and [[Jesus College, Oxford]].  He was awarded a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree by the [[University of Oxford]] in 1988.  In 1991 he was awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in [[physical chemistry]] for research supervised by {{ill|Gus Hancock|qid=Q56569326}},<ref name=frs/><ref>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|title=Laser studies of reaction dynamics|first= Andrew John|last=Orr-Ewing|date=1991|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.302888}}|url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph015984335|website=ox.ac.uk|oclc=53493953}}</ref> also at the University of Oxford.

==Career and research==
Following his DPhil, Orr-Ewing completed two years of [[post-doctoral research]] supervised by [[Richard Zare]] at [[Stanford University]] in California,<ref name=Orr-EwingZare1994>{{cite journal|last1=Orr-Ewing|first1=A J|last2=Zare|first2=R N|title=Orientation and Alignment of Reaction Products|journal=Annual Review of Physical Chemistry|volume=45|issue=1|year=1994|pages=315–366|issn=0066-426X|doi=10.1146/annurev.pc.45.100194.001531|bibcode=1994ARPC...45..315O}}</ref> and was then a [[Royal Society]] Elizabeth Challenor [[research fellow]] at the [[University of Bristol]], where he was later appointed [[Professor]] of physical chemistry in August 2004. His research interests are in [[physical chemistry]] and [[chemical physics]].<ref name=googlescholar/>

===Awards and honours===
Orr-Ewing has received awards from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] including the [[Edward Harrison Memorial Prize]] in 1994, the [[Marlow Medal]] in 1999, the [[Tilden Prize]] in 2009, the [[Faraday Lectureship Prize]] in 2026, and awards in [[optical spectroscopy]] in 2002 and [[chemical dynamics]] in 2014. He was a [[Leverhulme Trust]] senior [[research fellow]] in 2005, and received a [[Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Award]] in 2006.<ref name=frs/> He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2017|Fellow of the Royal Society in 2017]]<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/andrew-orr-ewing-10208/|website=royalsociety.org|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|author=Anon|year=2017|title=Professor Andrew Orr-Ewing FRS}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text under a [https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License].</ref> and a [[Member of the Academia Europaea]] (MAE) in 2018. In 2025, he was elected as a Foreign Fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]], and in 2026 as an International Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].
